content.title: Teaching in a Virtual Classroom: Live Online Teaching with Zoom-  Cycle 3
content.summary: The Network of Blended and Digital learning offered its 3rd Cycle of the Teaching in a Virtual Classroom: Live online Teaching with Zoom.

content.text: "The workshop was very well organized. The facilitators were also very helpful and the content delivery of the facilitators was in the right manner which made us understand the topic more". - Anjiya Nuruddin (Network of Quality, Teaching and Learning)

, 2020, the Network of Blended and Digital learning offered its third cycle of a two-day synchronous online workshop. 12 AKU faculty members and staff participated in the workshop from different entities including SONAM-East Africa, Medical College Pakistan, IED Pakistan, the Network of Quality, Teaching and Learning and staff from various departments.
This workshop aimed to enable faculty members to design and offer an engaging synchronous online teaching and learning session using Zoom.

The workshop began with facilitators and participants discussing the concept of online teaching and student engagement. This was followed by hands on practice of various features of through some fun interactive activities. Teaching effectively in an online classroom while keeping the learners engaged was modelled during the session along with giving participants a chance to discuss their concerns and queries. The session also provided participants an opportunity to design an online session plan incorporating an array of techniques and tools to engage their learners. Session concluded with participants presenting their plan which was followed by constructive feedback from the facilitators and their peers.

Participants left the workshop satisfied with a new and improved approach toward synchronous online teaching. The effectiveness of the sessions was clear as participants stated in their post-workshop evaluation.
"You have demystified online learning!" - Grace Nakate (SONAM, East Africa)
"Thank you very much it was a good learning experience!" - Sadia Masood (Medical College, Pakistan)
Overall the workshop was a success giving both participants and facilitators an opportunity to reflect and improve their future practices.
